name: GO Classes CS Test Series 2026 | Digital Logic | Topic Wise Test 2

question.text:
Consider the following combinational circuit using a decoder and OR gates, implementing three Boolean functions $\text{F}_{1}, \text{F}_{2}, \text{F}_{3}:$

For how many input combinations $(x,y,z),$ at least two of these boolean functions are high?

The figure above implements the Boolean function:

  1. $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})=\Sigma(2,3,5,6)$
  2. $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})=\Sigma(3,4,6,7)$
  3. $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})=\Sigma(1,3,6,7)$
  4. $\mathrm{F}(\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}, \mathrm{z})=\Sigma(0,2,4,6)$

A multiplexer, shown below on the right, has $6$ inputs, $S_0, S_1, A, B, C$, and $D.$ The truth table on the left describes its function.

It is desired to implement the function $F=(X \oplus Y) \oplus Z$ using the multiplexer. If $X$ is applied to $S_{0}$, and $Y$ is applied to $S_{1}$, what inputs should be applied to $A, B, C$ and $D$ to realize the function $F$?

  1. $A=B=C=D=Z$
  2. $A=X \oplus Y, B=X \oplus Z, C=Y \oplus Z, D=Z$
  3. $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Z} ; \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{C}=\overline{Z}$
  4. the function $F$ can not be realized with any of the inputs shown above.

Above circuit represents

  1. $2 \times 1$ MUX with $\text{A, B}$ as input lines and $\text{C}$ as a select line
  2. $4 \times 1$ MUX with $\text{A, B}$ as input lines and $\text{C}$ as a select line
  3. $2 \times 1$ MUX with $\text{A, C}$ as input lines and $\text{B}$ as a select line
  4. $4 \times 1 \mathrm{MUX}$ with $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{C}$ as input lines and $\mathrm{B}$ as a select line

As shown in the three diagrams below, device FA makes use of Two copies of device HA, and device D makes use of four copies of device FA. Assume that all basic logic gates(AND, OR, NOT, XOR gate) have the same delay T.

If all inputs to device D become available simultaneously, which output will be available last?

  1. $\text{S}_{1}$
  2. $\text{S}_{2}$
  3. $\text{S}_{3}$
  4. They will all be available simultaneously.

As shown in the three diagrams below, device FA makes use of Two copies of device HA, and device D makes use of four copies of device FA. Assume that all basic logic gates(AND, OR, NOT, XOR gate) have the same delay T.


If all inputs to device D become available simultaneously, the delay before $S_2$ must be valid is $kT,$ then what is $k?$

We design a comparator circuit that takes two $4$-bit words $a_{3} a_{2} a_{1} a_{0}$ and $b_{3} b_{2} b_{1} b_{0}$ as inputs, and generates one output $f$ which is $1$ iff the two words are identical, i.e. $a_{i}=b_{i, \text { for all four bits }}$ $(i=0,1,2,3)$. Then which of the following is NOT a correct expression for $f?$

  1. $\overline{\left(a_{3} \oplus b_{3}\right)+\left(a_{2} \oplus b_{2}\right)+\left(a_{1} \oplus b_{1}\right)+\left(a_{0} \oplus b_{0}\right)}$
  2. $\left(a_{3} \odot b_{3}\right)\left(a_{2} \odot b_{2}\right)\left(a_{1} \odot b_{1}\right)\left(a_{0} \odot b_{0}\right)$
  3. $\left(a_{3} \odot b_{3}\right)+\left(a_{2} \odot b_{2}\right)+\left(a_{1} \odot b_{1}\right)+\left(a_{0} \odot b_{0}\right)$
  4. $\left(\overline{a_{3}} \oplus b_{3}\right)\left(\overline{a_{2}} \oplus b_{2}\right)\left(\overline{a_{1}} \oplus b_{1}\right)\left(\overline{a_{0}} \oplus b_{0}\right)$

Consider the following combinational circuit using a decoder and OR gates, implementing three Boolean functions $\text{F}_1, \text{F}_2, \text{F}_3:$

Which of the following is/are correct boolean expressions for these boolean functions?

  1. $\mathrm{F}_{1}=\mathrm{x}^{\prime} \mathrm{y}^{\prime} \mathrm{z}+\mathrm{xz'}$
  2. $\mathrm{F}_{2}=\mathrm{x}^{\prime} \mathrm{yz'}$ $+\mathrm{xy}$ '
  3. $\mathrm{F}_{3}=\mathrm{xyz'}+\mathrm{xz}$
  4. $\mathrm{F}_{3} = \mathrm x' y z + \mathrm x y$

Which of the following is the correct function for Full adder where inputs ' $a$ ' and '$b$' are the numbers added, and input '$c$' is the carry-in. Also, '$s$' and '$co$' are sum and carry out, respectively.

  1. $c o=b c+a c+a b ; s=a$ xor $b$ xor $c$
  2. $c o=b ' c+a ' c+a b ; s=a$ xor b xor $c$
  3. $c o=b c+a c+a ' b ' ; s=a$ xor b xor $c$
  4. $c o=b c+a c+a b ; s=(a b)$ xor $c$

An $8 \times 1$ multiplexer has inputs $\text{A, B}$ and $\text{C}$ connected to the selection inputs $\text{S}_{2}(\text{MSB}), \text{S}_{1}$, and $\text{S}_{0}(\text{LSB})$ respectively. The data inputs through $I_{0}$ through $\mathrm{I}_{7}$ are as follows:
$$\mathrm{I}_{1}=\mathrm{I}_{2}=\mathrm{I}_{4}=0 ; \mathrm{I}_{3}=\mathrm{I}_{5}=1 ; \mathrm{I}_{0}=\mathrm{I}_{7}=\mathrm{D} ; \;\text{and}\; \mathrm{I}_{6}=\overline{\text{D}}$$
Consider the Boolean function $\text{F(A, B, C, D)}$ that this multiplexer implements.

How many minterms of $F$ are there for which $\text{F}$ is $1?$

The logic circuit above is used to compare two unsigned $2$-bit numbers,

$\mathrm{X}_{1} \mathrm{X}_{0}=\mathrm{X}$ and $\text{Y}_{1} \text{Y}_{0}=\text{Y}$, where $\text{X}_{0}$ and $\text{Y}_{0}$ are the least significant bits. (A small circle on any line in a logic diagram indicates logical NOT.)

Which of the following always makes the output $\text{Z}$ have the value $1?$

  1. $\text{X}>\text{Y}$
  2. $\text{X}<\text{Y}$
  3. $\text{X} \neq \text{Y}$
  4. $\text{X} \geq \text{Y}$
